title: Badges
reviewHint: A reviewer awards this badge. The clear video needs to show a webcam.

help.title: Badge engine
help.subtitle: Every list, field, and structure a grant script can use.

lists.title: Lists
lists.intro: These names are always in scope. Each item is a row of fields. A placeholder 5/40/5 sheet keeps its chart fields, but its accuracy and judgement fields are empty.

mine.title: Credited or cleared charts
mine.desc: Charts this creator is credited on, or charts this player has cleared. Same fields as levels.

ratings.title: Ratings
ratings.desc: Rows of levelId and week for ratings by this user.

clearFields.title: Clear fields
clearFields.intro: Read these from a row in clears. Names are case-sensitive.

levelId.title: Chart id
levelId.desc: Number. The chart this clear is on.

identity.title: Identity key
identity.desc: Text. Charts collapsed by the badge identity share one key.

speed.title: Speed
speed.desc: Number, such as 1 or 2. Null when the clear has no speed.

difficulty.title: Current difficulty
difficulty.desc: Text. The chart's difficulty name now, such as G10.

difficultyAt.title: Difficulty at upload
difficultyAt.desc: Text. The difficulty name when the clear was uploaded.

family.title: Current family
family.desc: Text. The family of the current difficulty, such as G, U, GQ, UQ, or QQ.

song.title: Song title
song.desc: Text. Empty when the chart has no song title.

durationMs.title: Length
durationMs.desc: Chart length in milliseconds, or null.

accuracy.title: Accuracy ratio
accuracy.desc: Number from 0 to 1. Null on a placeholder sheet.

accuracyText.title: Displayed accuracy
accuracyText.desc: Text such as 99.995, using the same formatter as the site. Empty on a placeholder sheet.

score.title: Score
score.desc: Score v2 as a number. Null on a placeholder sheet.

scoreText.title: Displayed score
scoreText.desc: Score fixed to 3 decimals, such as 100.000.

worldsFirst.title: 1.0× world first
worldsFirst.desc: True only when speed is exactly 1 and the live world-first flag is set.

isWorldsFirst.title: World-first flag
isWorldsFirst.desc: The raw flag at any speed. It does not require speed 1.

worldsFirstPP.title: PP world first
worldsFirstPP.desc: True when this clear holds the world-first pure perfect.

ancient.title: Placeholder sheet
ancient.desc: True for the 5/40/5 placeholder. Accuracy and judgement fields are then empty.

xPerfect.title: X-perfect mode
xPerfect.desc: True when the clear was played in X-perfect mode.

reference.title: Reference chart
reference.desc: True when the chart is a reference chart.

curation.title: Curation names
curation.desc: List of text, such as C3 or V3. Use .includes.

charterCount.title: Charter count
charterCount.desc: How many charters are credited on the chart.

vfxerCount.title: VFXer count
vfxerCount.desc: How many VFXers are credited on the chart.

ownerIsCharter.title: Owner is charter
ownerIsCharter.desc: True when this creator, or the player as a creator, is a charter of the chart.

ownerIsVfxer.title: Owner is VFXer
ownerIsVfxer.desc: True when this creator is a VFXer of the chart.

noPriorClear.title: First clear of the identity
noPriorClear.desc: True on the earliest clear of that identity with a known upload time.

month.title: Upload month
month.desc: UTC month, 1 through 12. Null when the upload time is unknown.

day.title: Upload day
day.desc: UTC day of the month. Null when the upload time is unknown.

uploadMs.title: Upload time
uploadMs.desc: Upload time in milliseconds, or null when it is unknown.

examples.worldsFirst: clear.worldsFirst == true is a 1.0× world first. clear.isWorldsFirst is the flag at any speed.
examples.accuracyText: clear.accuracyText.endsWith("31") matches the displayed accuracy, not the raw ratio.

judgements.title: Judgement fields
judgements.intro: These are empty on a placeholder or all-zero sheet. A missing bucket counts as 0. Too-late is not a field here.

perfects.title: Perfect total
perfects.desc: Center perfects, plus perfect-minus and perfect-plus in X-perfect mode.

ppMinusOne.title: One off pure
ppMinusOne.desc: True when exactly one judgement is outside the perfect band and there are no misses.

noMisses.title: No misses
noMisses.desc: True when misses are 0 and the sheet is not empty.

symmetry.title: Symmetric spread
symmetry.desc: True when early singles equal late singles and early perfects equal late perfects, and the clear is not a pure perfect.

technicallyPure.title: Technically pure
technicallyPure.desc: True when there are no early or late perfects, and both an early single and a late single.

noPerfects.title: No perfects
noPerfects.desc: True when the perfect total is 0 and the sheet is not empty.

asymmetry.title: Asymmetric spread
asymmetry.desc: True when some non-perfect bucket is larger than the perfect total.

examples.symmetry: clear.symmetry == true && (clear.familyAt == "G" || clear.familyAt == "U") keeps symmetric G or U clears.
examples.ppMinusOne: clear.ppMinusOne == true is one judgement outside the perfect band and zero misses.

levelFields.title: Chart fields
levelFields.intro: Read these from a row in levels or mine.

identity.title: Identity key
identity.desc: Text. Same collapse rules as a clear.

clears.title: Clear count
clears.desc: How many public clears the chart has.

reference.title: Reference chart
reference.desc: True when the chart is a reference chart.

ownerIsCharter.title: Owner is charter
ownerIsCharter.desc: True when this creator chartered the chart.

ownerIsVfxer.title: Owner is VFXer
ownerIsVfxer.desc: True when this creator is a VFXer.

artistIds.title: Artist ids
artistIds.desc: List of artist ids on the song.

rivals.title: Other players
rivals.desc: How many other players have a non-placeholder clear.

structures.title: Structures
structures.intro: The script uses JavaScript shape. It does not run arbitrary JavaScript. // line comments and /* */ block comments are skipped.

eq.title: Equal
eq.desc: == and a single = compare loosely. === compares strictly. Text is case-sensitive.

not.title: Not
not.desc: ! flips a condition. != and !== are the negated comparisons.

arrow.title: Function
arrow.desc: item => item.speed >= 2 is a function. { return ... } is also allowed.

filter.title: Keep rows
filter.example: clears.filter(clear => clear.difficultyAt == "G10") keeps only the G10 clears.

map.title: Transform rows
map.example: clears.map(clear => clear.levelId) is the list of chart ids, one per clear.

some.title: Any match
some.desc: .some(item => ...) is true when one row matches.
some.example: clears.some(clear => clear.misses > 75) is true when any clear has more than 75 misses.

every.title: All match
every.desc: .every(item => ...) is true when every row matches. An empty list is true.
every.example: ["C1", "C2"].every(name => mine.some(level => level.curation.includes(name))) is true only when both curations are present.

find.title: First match
find.desc: .find(item => ...) returns the first matching row, or null.
find.example: clears.find(clear => clear.levelId == 1) is the first clear of chart 1, or null.

includes.title: Contains
includes.desc: On a list, .includes(value). On text, .includes, .startsWith, and .endsWith.
includes.example: clear.curation.includes("V3") is true when that chart has a V3 curation.

length.title: Size
length.desc: .length on a list or on text. count(list) is the same size for a list.
length.example: clears.length is how many clears there are. "G10".length is 3.

text.title: Text case
text.example: "WYSI".toLowerCase() is wysi. clear.accuracyText.endsWith("31") checks the displayed accuracy.

optional.title: Missing field
optional.desc: row?.field is null when the row is null, instead of failing.

examples.text: clear.song.toLowerCase().includes("wysi") matches the song title without case.

numbers.title: Number functions
numbers.intro: These turn rows or numbers into one number. A missing number counts as 0 inside arithmetic.

count.title: How many
count.desc: count(list) is the number of rows. The rows it counts are the clears shown on the badge.
count.example: count(clears.filter(clear => clear.speed >= 2)) is 4 when four clears are at 2.0× or faster.

distinct.title: One per key
distinct.desc: distinct(list, item => item.identity) keeps the first row of each key.
distinct.example: distinct(clears, clear => clear.identity) keeps one row when the same chart was cleared twice.

sum.title: Add
sum.desc: sum(list) adds the numbers. sum(list, item => item.speed) adds a field.
sum.example: sum([1, 0.5, 0.5]) is 2. sum(clears, clear => clear.speed) adds every speed.

min.title: Smallest
min.desc: min(list) or min(list, item => item.keyCount). min(a, b) compares two numbers.
min.example: min(4, 1) is 1. min(clears.map(clear => clear.keyCount)) is the lowest key count.

max.title: Largest
max.example: max(3, 9) is 9. max(mine.map(level => level.clears)) is the busiest chart.

threshold.title: Reached a cutoff
threshold.desc: threshold(n, 10) is 1 when n is at least 10, otherwise 0.

examples.distinct: count(distinct(clears.filter(clear => clear.speed >= 2), clear => clear.identity)) counts charts cleared at 2.0× or faster, once each.

curves.title: Curves and results
curves.intro: The script should return a tier. A curve turns a count into tiers and sets the progress bar.

curve.title: Climbing tiers
curve.desc: curve(credit, start, step) earns a tier at start, then start plus step, and so on.
curve.example: curve(30, 10, 20) is tier 2: 10 earns tier 1 and 30 earns tier 2.

curveDown.title: Descending tiers
curveDown.desc: curveDown(credit, start, step) earns a tier at start, then start minus step.
curveDown.example: curveDown(2, 4, 1) is tier 3, stepping from 4 down through 3 to 2.

result.title: Set the tier and the bar
result.desc: result(tier, credit, from, to) sets them directly, so a partial count does not earn a tier by itself.
result.example: result(0, 6, 0, 8) stays at tier 0 while the bar shows 6 of 8.

number.title: Plain number
number.desc: A number of 1 or more is itself the tier. Anything smaller is tier 0.

examples.up: curve(count(clears), 10, 20) earns tier 1 at 10 clears, then every 20.
examples.down: curveDown(min(clears.map(clear => clear.keyCount)), 4, 1) starts at 4 keys and steps down.
examples.result: result(ratio >= 0.75 ? 1 : 0, cleared, 0, total) shows the count and awards the tier only at 75%.

functions.title: Host functions
functions.intro: These read this player, this creator, or other players.

difficulty.title: One difficulty
difficulty.example: difficulty("G10").cleared is 6 when six G10 charts are cleared. .ratio is cleared divided by total.

sequence.title: Ordered chart ids
sequence.desc: sequence([id, id]) walks clears in upload order and returns how many ids matched in order.
sequence.example: sequence([5017, 52]) is 2 when chart 52 is cleared after 5017. It is 1 when only 5017 has been cleared.

consecutive.title: Order with no gap
consecutive.desc: consecutive([id, id], item => item.ppMinusOne) is the same walk, each step must pass the test, and the clears must be consecutive.
consecutive.example: consecutive([5017, 52], clear => clear.ppMinusOne) is 2 only when those PP-1 clears follow each other with nothing uploaded between them.

blocks.title: Id blocks
blocks.desc: blocks(10, "Impossible", "Censored") returns how many complete id blocks of that size exist, skipping those difficulties.
blocks.example: blocks(10, "Impossible", "Censored") is 1 when every other chart in ids 1–10 is cleared. It stops at the first unfinished block.

prefix.title: Leading set
prefix.desc: prefix("planetary") counts how far a named difficulty set is cleared from the start, using difficulty at upload.
prefix.example: prefix("planetary") is 3 when P1, P2, and P3 were the difficulties at upload, and P4 was not cleared.

gap.title: Longest gap
gap.desc: gap() is the longest gap in days between clears of the same identity.
gap.example: gap() is 730 when the longest gap between two clears of the same chart is 730 days.

pack.title: Pack chart ids
pack.desc: pack() is the chart ids in this badge's pack. A chart listed twice counts once.
pack.example: count(pack()) is 12 when the pack lists 12 charts. A chart listed twice still counts once.

complete.title: Charted set
complete.desc: complete("end-to-end") is 1 when this creator has charted every difficulty in the named set.
complete.example: complete("end-to-end") is 1 only when this creator has charted every difficulty in that set. Otherwise it is 0.

nth.title: Nth clearer
nth.desc: nth(100) counts charts where this player was the 100th distinct clearer.
nth.example: nth(100) is 2 when this player was the 100th distinct clearer on two charts.

lead.title: Current lead
lead.desc: lead(level, "accuracy") is true when this player leads that chart. The metric is accuracy, score, or speed.
lead.example: lead(level, "score") is true when this player's score on that chart is the highest.

first.title: Any-speed world first
first.desc: first(level) is true when this player has the raw world-first flag on that chart.
first.example: first(level) is true when this player holds the world-first flag on that chart, even at a speed other than 1.0×.

shared.title: Shared accuracy
shared.desc: shared() counts galactic or universal charts where this player's displayed accuracy also appears on another chart.
shared.example: shared() is 1 when this player's displayed accuracy on a G or U chart also appears on a different chart.

inSet.title: Named set
inSet.desc: inSet(clear.difficultyAt, "planetary") is true when the value is in that named set.

maxGroup.title: Largest group
maxGroup.desc: maxGroup(rows, "artistIds", "songId") is the most distinct values grouped by the first field.
maxGroup.example: maxGroup(mine, "artistIds", "songId") is 20 when one artist has 20 songs charted by this creator.

examples.sequence: sequence([5017, 52]) == 2 means those two charts were cleared in that upload order.
examples.lead: count(levels.filter(level => level.family == "G" && lead(level, "accuracy"))) counts galactic charts where this player leads accuracy.

clears.title: Public clears
clears.intro: The engine only sees passes and charts that are public.

bullets.visible: Hidden and deleted passes and charts are skipped. Wrong-judgement passes stay.
bullets.buckets: A missing judgement bucket counts as 0.
bullets.worldsFirst: A world-first check also requires speed exactly 1, then follows the live flag. The flag moves when an earlier 1.0x upload is accepted.
bullets.placeholder: The 5/40/5 placeholder sheet is skipped by anything that reads judgements, accuracy, or score. An all-zero sheet is ignored the same way.
bullets.unknownTime: Upload times 2023-01-01 07:27:27 and 2023-07-27 07:27:27 are unknown. gap, sequence, nth, and earned-time ordering skip them.

identity.title: Chart identity
identity.intro: Identity decides whether linked charts count as one chart or many.

level.title: Chart id
level.desc: Each chart id is its own chart.

chartSubgroup.title: Charter subgroup
chartSubgroup.desc: Linked charts that share a charter subgroup collapse into one.

vfxSubgroup.title: VFX subgroup
vfxSubgroup.desc: Linked charts that share a VFX subgroup collapse into one.

group.title: Link group
group.desc: The whole link group collapses into one.

bullets.ownChart: A clear only contributes its own chart's key count, difficulty, and curation. Clearing the unlimited sibling does not inherit the 10-key chart's key count.
bullets.reclear: For a collapsed identity, the sibling clear is a reclear, not a second chart.

history.title: Difficulty at the time
history.intro: difficultyAt uses the chart's difficulty when the pass was uploaded.

bullets.walk: The engine walks rerate history against the upload time. Before the first recorded change, the difficulty is that row's previous difficulty.
bullets.fallback: With no history, the clear-time snapshot is used, then the chart's current difficulty.
bullets.snapshot: A snapshot is written when a pass is accepted or a world-first flag is refreshed. It stores difficulty, base score, PP base score, curation type ids, and charter and VFXer ids.
bullets.older: Older passes stay on the current difficulty until something rewrites them.

grants.title: Grant modes
grants.intro: The grant mode decides whether a tier can be lost.

live.title: Recompute
live.desc: The tier is recalculated and can be lost.

persistTier.title: Keep the best tier
persistTier.desc: The highest tier reached is kept.

persistSnapshot.title: Freeze the set
persistSnapshot.desc: The chart set that satisfied a percent badge stays frozen, so later charts do not raise the denominator.

resetOnGrowth.title: Live target
resetOnGrowth.desc: The pack default. A chart added to the pack removes completion until it is cleared.

manualLock.title: Needs a review
manualLock.desc: Stays off until a reviewer approves a video.

chase.title: Store a number
chase.desc: Keeps the current number, such as the lowest uncleared chart id.

bullets.replace: Saving a definition keeps persistTier and persistSnapshot results unless Replace earned tiers is on.

backfill.title: Backfill
backfill.intro: Backfill decides which existing clears are eligible when the badge is published. Adding a badge later uses the same job.

queue.title: Reviews only
queue.desc: Creates review rows and does not grant, except a manualLock badge, which grants after approval.

bullets.skips: The job records how many passes it skipped for a placeholder sheet, an unknown upload time, or a missing difficulty history.
bullets.unreconstructed: Facts that were never stored, such as curation at the moment of an old clear, cannot be reconstructed.

reviews.title: Reviews and secrecy
reviews.intro: Reviews gate manual badges. Secrecy controls what a locked badge shows.

bullets.video: Approving a review requires a video URL and records the reviewer.
bullets.secret: Unearned secret badges are omitted from profiles.
bullets.locked: Other unearned badges show a name, icon, and progress bar, including the next number, but not the requirement text or the expression.
bullets.earned: After a badge is earned, its tier label and proving passes are shown.
bullets.confirm: accuracyFull and judgementsFull add server-rendered confirm text on that badge only. Public score cards keep the normal accuracy formatter.
